transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-09-02 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Ramos (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Gomez (Redwood SA); Jordan Lee (CTO, MerKury), Priya Nair (CISO), Mateo Ruiz (Platform), Elaine Chen (Legal)

Summary (auto): high-level security review focused on data residency, sub-processors, encryption/K M S key control and support access.

[00:00] Alex Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Jordan Lee: Jordan here.
[00:09] Priya Nair: Priya on for security.
[00:11] Mateo Ruiz: Mateo.
[00:13] Elaine Chen: Elaine from legal.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Samir, Redwood SE.
[00:18] Alex Ramos: Great. We'll run through region pinning and data flow controls, then dig into KMS and subprocessors. Nina will jump in for any arch diagrams.

[03:02] Samir Patel: To start, our platform supports three deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, and private V P C. For strict EU-only processing you generally want Dedicated in eu-west or our Private VPC installed in your cloud. There is a region-affinity policy that pins inference to a region and blocks fallback to other regions unless you opt in.
[05:45] Priya Nair: Clarify "blocks fallback" — if we hit capacity in eu-west, we cannot let requests spill to US. Is that enforced at routing layer or by contract?
[06:10] Samir Patel: Good question. Technically the smart router prefers the pinned region; by default there's a hard-safety that prevents cross-region routing for requests tagged as "EU-only". We can also set a contractual SLA clause that prohibits cross-border processing for those datasets. However, note that our hosted fallback options can be configured for availability but are off for strict EU controls.
[08:20] Jordan Lee: We run EU customer PII and transaction logs in S3 eu-west-1 and want to guarantee those never go to any US sub-processor. Who's on your subprocessor list now?
[08:39] Alex Ramos: We'll send the current subprocessor spreadsheet — it includes infra partners, monitoring, and backup providers. Off the top: our compute partners, metrics provider, and a couple of managed DB vendors.
[09:12] Elaine Chen: We need the list with locations (region) and contractual restrictions. Also, are your subprocessors bound by the same region-pinning obligations?
[09:34] Nina Gomez: Subprocessors are contractually obligated for customer-data handling as per the DPA, but some of them have global footprints; we can indicate which ones will process EU-only workloads.
[10:05] Priya Nair: Regarding K M S — BYOK is non-negotiable for us for encryption at rest. We don't want Redwood or any subprocessor to have plaintext access. How do you handle key material?
[10:33] Samir Patel: We support customer-managed keys in major cloud K M S systems (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). With BYOK, the key is stored in your KMS and tokens are used for wrap/unwrap; Redwood never stores the unencrypted key. Support access to logs or debug artifacts can be configured to never include plaintext.
[11:22] Mateo Ruiz: For the inference workloads, do you hold any decrypted model state or KV cache that could include sensitive tokens? We're concerned about ephemeral state in memory or disk.
[11:39] Samir Patel: The KV cache is in-memory on the inference nodes and is not persisted by default. For Dedicated/Private modes you control the hardware or V P C and can apply disk encryption policies. We can also scrub caches after request completion; we have short TTL defaults.
[13:00] Jordan Lee: Is there any possibility of support engineers from Redwood accessing customer data during incident response?
[13:18] Alex Ramos: Access is RBAC-controlled; support access requires just-in-time elevation and is logged. We can provide audit logs showing any session activity. For EU-only accounts we can restrict support access to tokenized meta-data only.
[13:45] Priya Nair: Do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates? We'll need copies.
[13:51] Alex Ramos: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO27001. We'll share redacted reports — standard.
[14:20] Elaine Chen: Also need to see the K M S integration diagram and the key rotation policy. Any chance those are in your security pack?
[14:29] Nina Gomez: They are; I'll include the K M S diagram and the BYOK flow in the pack Sam will send.
[16:05] Mateo Ruiz: For network egress, how do you prove that traffic never left eu-west? Are your routers in-region single-tenant or shared?
[16:25] Samir Patel: For Dedicated capacity in a region we use tenant-isolated GPU pools. For hosted accounts we do multi-tenant but region pinned. We can provide VPC flow logs, and exportable network traces showing egress endpoints.
[18:00] Jordan Lee: We also want to restrict metadata or embeddings generated from EU datasets — are embeddings ever used for cross-customer caching?
[18:20] Samir Patel: Embedding caching is per-customer and tied to region. By default we don't replicate across regions. If you require, we can disable cross-region cache replication entirely for your account.
[19:10] Priya Nair: Legal question — under the DPA we want a clause that requires Redwood to notify us within 72 hours if a subprocessor changes location or adds cross-border processing. Can you accept that?
[19:36] Elaine Chen: (interject) We'll propose the exact DPA text but want a 72-hour notification plus 30-day mitigation plan.
[19:47] Alex Ramos: That's reasonable, we'll push that to legal.
[21:00] Samir Patel: One nuance — if you choose the Private on-prem package, you get the strongest guarantees: no Redwood-managed subprocessors touching compute, but we still offer the control plane options. If you want no external subprocessor on compute, Private is the path.
[22:15] Jordan Lee: But private on-prem is heavy lift. We're exploring dedicated eu-west but with BYOK and strict subprocessors list. Can you do that?
[22:36] Samir Patel: Yes; dedicated eu-west with BYOK and contractual region-pinning is a common enterprise configuration.
[24:10] Mateo Ruiz: For compliance evidence, can we get sample audit logs that show RBAC elevations and K M S key use? Format like CSV preferred for ingestion.
[24:32] Nina Gomez: We can export audit logs with timestamps, actor, action, and region. We'll provide an example export.
[25:40] Priya Nair: A few nitpicks: SSO — do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning? Role mappings for RBAC?
[26:05] Alex Ramos: Yes SAML 2.0 S A M L and SCIM for provisioning. Our RBAC supports hierarchical roles and we can map IdP groups to roles.
[27:40] Jordan Lee: Is there any telemetry or metadata that you consider "service usage" which might include token hashes or truncated data we should worry about?
[27:58] Samir Patel: We capture request metadata for billing and routing — e.g., request size, timestamp, model id — but we can disable retention for request payloads for EU-only accounts.
[29:10] Elaine Chen: Regarding subprocessors — do you allow contractual carve-outs where a named subprocessor is permitted only for non-EU data? We might accept that as long as it's explicit.
[29:30] Alex Ramos: Yes, we can state per-subprocessor region scoping in the DPA annex.
[31:00] Mateo Ruiz: About encryption in transit: are you using mTLS between components and do you provide cert transparency logs?
[31:20] Samir Patel: All internal RPCs use mTLS and we can provide cert thumbprints in audit logs. External API endpoints are HTTPS/TLS 1.3 and support client certs for dedicated/private deployments.
[33:00] Priya Nair: For incident response, what's your runbook if an EU data exposure is suspected?
[33:20] Alex Ramos: We have an IR plan — notify customer within 24 hours for critical incidents, contain, engage forensic, and provide a remediation timeline. For EU-specific exposures we escalate to our privacy team. We'll share the IR playbook redacted.
[34:50] Jordan Lee: A practical question: when we tag datasets as EU-only, what's the config surface? Is it per-route, per-bucket, or per-request header?
[35:10] Samir Patel: You can do all three. Common pattern: tag input at the route level (API token associated with account + policy), or pass a header x-redwood-region: eu to enforce. We recommend account-level pinning for consistency.
[36:40] Mateo Ruiz: Are there any metrics we lose by disabling cross-region fallback — e.g., availability SLOs?
[36:58] Samir Patel: You may see reduced cross-region availability during regional outages, so you trade some global failover for strict residency. Our SLA for Dedicated has regional uptime targets; we can provide historical availability by region.
[38:05] Elaine Chen: How does your change-management notify customers about subprocessor changes? Do you have an automated feed or mailing list?
[38:21] Nina Gomez: We have an automated subprocessor notice email plus a PSR (public subprocessor registry) that we update; for customers requiring stricter notice we'll add the 72-hour contractual requirement.
[39:50] Jordan Lee: For K M S key rotation — if we rotate a key, does it break in-flight sessions or cached model state?
[40:06] Samir Patel: Rotation uses wrap/unwrap semantics; new requests get wrapped with the new key but existing tokens remain usable until expiration to avoid disruption. We coordinate key rotations; with BYOK you control rotation windows.
[42:10] Priya Nair: One more on logging — we need immutable archive of audit logs stored in EU for 7+ years. Are you able to dump logs to our S3 bucket in eu-west-1?
[42:30] Samir Patel: Yes, we support log export to customer-owned storage (S3, GCS) in region. We can set lifecycle and retention per your policy.
[44:00] Alex Ramos: Quick run-through of next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs and subprocessor list; Samir will prepare region-pinning runbook and a short terraform snippet for pinning routes; Nina will include K M S diagram.
[44:18] Elaine Chen: Legal will draft DPA redlines and propose 72-hour notification clause.
[44:30] Jordan Lee: We'll prepare a list of dataset tags that must remain EU-only and circulate to Redwood before the deep dive.
[45:05] Mateo Ruiz: Also request a short POC — dedicated eu-west trial for 2 weeks to run our workload.
[45:22] Samir Patel: We can provision a trial Dedicated cluster for tests; I'll coordinate quotas and costs with Alex.
[46:50] Priya Nair: Can you also include a short demo of audit log exports during the technical deep dive?
[47:10] Nina Gomez: Absolutely.
[49:00] Jordan Lee: Anything else on the legal side?
[49:15] Elaine Chen: We'll want indemnity language and clarity on subprocessors access to debug artifacts.
[49:40] Alex Ramos: We'll include that in the DPA conversation.
[51:00] Samir Patel: Minor caveat — some third-party monitoring vendors do ingest aggregated metrics; if those are EU-only we mark them as in-region partners. We'll mark them in the spreadsheet.
[52:10] Jordan Lee: Good. If we get the SOC2 and K M S docs by Wednesday, we can aim to have legal redlines the following week.
[52:25] Elaine Chen: Yes, that's our plan.
[54:00] Alex Ramos: Wrap up — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and book the deep dive.
[54:12] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[54:15] Jordan Lee: Thanks all.
[57:30] (Call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: Some acronyms mis-transcribed (K M S, S A M L, V P C), occasional timestamp drift from auto-transcript.
